text:
Alex: FYI — customer AcmeCorp reporting sustained 502/504s from hosted generate since ~11:45 UTC, ~20% of requests failing. Sample request_id: abcdef1234. @Nate can you pick this up?

Nate: On it. Is this streaming or non-streaming, and can you paste a curl we can repro with?

Alex: Non-streaming /v1/generate. They hit via SDK v0.9.2 and directly with curl. Example payload: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hi","request_id":"abcdef1234"}'
```
Response: 502 Bad Gateway, body: {"error":"upstream_error","code":502}.

Priya: Pulled ingress logs for request_id=abcdef1234 — backend 10.12.45.8 returned 504 after ~30s. Edge shows connection reset during drain window.

Jamie: We kicked a rolling drain on node pool hosted-gen-usw2-pool-B at 11:40 for a kernel patch. Possible correlation — edge should route around, but I'm seeing a spike in hot-prefix concurrency -> kvcache lock contention.

Priya: I repro'ed locally from curl (us-west) and saw 502 ~3/10 attempts. Runtime trace: KVCache fetch blocked on shard lock ~28s, then upstream timed out.

Alex: This is customer-impacting (SLA 99.9). ETA and mitigation?

Jamie: Immediate mitigation: pause/rollback the drain on pool-B and lower drain concurrency. I'll start rollback now. @deploy-bot start rollback hosted-gen-usw2-pool-B

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for pool hosted-gen-usw2-pool-B — estimated completion 3m.

Priya: After rollback started, error rate dropped from ~20% -> ~1.5% over 2m. Trending down.

Nate: Sent interim customer update: "We're investigating elevated 502/504s during node updates; mitigation in progress and we've applied a rollback. Will send another update in 15 minutes."

Katie: Can we get a one-line status blurb for status.redwood.ai?

Jamie: Suggested blurb: "Partial request failures (502/504) observed during node rollouts affecting hosted generate in US-WEST2. Mitigation (rollback) applied; monitoring for recovery."

Priya: Root cause looks like interaction between node drain + hot KVCACHE shard locks leading to upstream timeouts. Next steps: add per-shard lock timeout metric, reduce drift during drains, implement warm-start KVCaches and fallback path to bypass lock for small reads. Opening runtime ticket now.

Alex: Good. Nate/Katie please confirm customer follow-up when fully recovered. We'll need a postmortem.

Nate: Update sent at 11:55 UTC — customer acknowledged and requested postmortem.

Priya: Created ticket INF-2026-042 with logs, sample requests, repro steps, and suggested mitigations.

Alex: Thanks all — closing thread unless errors resurge.
